content:
A few months ago at the FRO we noticed that upgrading from Linux 6.14 to 6.15 or later causes probablistic segfaults while compiling big Lean projects on certain AMD CPUs. We narrowed this bug down to be related to hardware based page invalidation and reported it to the Linux kernel . It turned out to be an actual AMD CPU bug! Linux 7.3, which was released just last week, contains a workaround for this bug, AMD is also starting to roll out microcode updates now. If you are:

  1. using a Linux kernel version >= 6.15 and <= 7.2 (more specifically a kernel that was built with CONFIG_BROADCAST_TLB_FLUSH=y)
  2. you have an AMD Zen 5 CPU (most people probably do not have such a new CPU so this is mostly a concern for high end server hardware users from the industry)

You should consider updating to kernel 7.3 and/or acquiring the latest AMD microcode. If for some reason you cannot upgrade to kernel 7.3 you should instead boot your kernel with the option tlbi=ipi.

It is possible that the bug affects older AMD CPUs going back as far as Zen 3 but unfortunately AMD has not yet publicly released the associated erratum (erratum number 1718 if someone reading this happens to have access :wink:)
